content.text: I couldn't see the defective code, so this diagnosis is an inference. The retrieved snippets don't include `AuthService.validateSocialLogin`, and I had no tool to open the file. The line numbers are estimates, based on `register` starting at line 200 and the social-login method sitting before it.

candidates.explanation: I think this is where an existing email/password account gets taken over. The method looks the user up by email, and when it finds one it appears to reuse that user and set its provider and socialId to the social provider's values. It does this without checking that the account is already active, confirmed and password-based. A local account that signs in with Google once ends up with provider 'google'. Email login then rejects it with 'needLoginViaProvider: google'. An active account with provider 'email' should not be relinked or overwritten by social sign-in.

This is the secondary place the symptom shows up. It refuses email login whenever user.provider !== 'email' and returns the message telling the user to log in via the provider. It only fails because the provider was overwritten earlier, so the real defect is upstream in the social login flow.

fix.description: In validateSocialLogin, when no user matches the social ID and provider but one matches by email, do not change that user's provider or socialId. If the existing account is an active email/password account, reject the social login with a conflict or unauthorized error, or only link it explicitly after the user has verified ownership. Social sign-in should only reuse accounts that already have the same provider, or create a new one when no account exists for the email.
